title: Anima vs. X-on Health: AI telephone reception for GP practices
summary: Compare Anima AI receptionist and X-on Health Voice Agent for GP telephone requests and workflow handoff, with FAQs on integration and switching.
body_markdown:
## What is AI telephone reception?


AI telephone reception collects a caller’s request and passes the information into the practice’s working process. Its purpose is to help patients make contact and reduce routine call-handling work, while preserving a clear route to staff when needed. A completed call should leave your team with a clear request and the information to respond.


Anima, X-on Health Voice Agent, QuantumLoopAI’s EMMA and InTouchNow AI handle patient calls using AI. This comparison covers Anima AI receptionist and X-on Health’s inbound Voice Agent. Surgery Connect, the wider telephone system that Voice Agent works within, has a separate role.


## Comparing Anima and X-on Health


X-on Health describes its inbound Voice Agent as an option within Surgery Connect that captures structured requests. Patients can choose the automated route or speak to reception. Compare this request-capture workflow with Anima’s AI receptionist and confirm how each would connect to your existing telephone and consultation systems.

## FAQs


### How do Surgery Connect, Phonebar and an AI receptionist differ?


Surgery Connect is a GP telephone system. Phonebar is its desktop tool for calls and patient communication. An AI receptionist for GP practices adds a different function: gathering the caller’s request. GP telephone triage still needs a clear handoff to the practice team. A voice agent adds a conversational workflow to capture or handle a request. Confirm whether the proposed agent needs a particular telephony product and which parts of your existing setup would change.


### What should you test before introducing an AI receptionist?


Try routine enquiries, unclear audio, pauses and callers who ask to speak to a person. Follow each completed call into the staff workflow and check whether the captured information is sufficient to act on. Agree how incomplete calls, outages and requests needing attention will be handled.


### How should you compare telephone reception costs?


Ask about call volumes, usage charges, telephone-system requirements, configuration and ongoing support. Compare the complete setup your practice needs. Measure the work left for reception after the call, as well as the time spent answering it.


## Are you planning a change in telephone reception?


Start with the patient journeys and call types your reception team handles today. Agree the route to human support, the destination of captured requests and the implementation steps with your telephone provider.
